text:
Alex: FYI production job hit repeated transient OOMs on a 8xA100 TP config. different from previous, this looks tied to kernel re-selection + sudden batching spikes when many short and a few long sequences interleave.

Mira: saw that pattern on the perf rig. profiling shows we momentarily allocate big comm scratch during kernel swap (fp16->int8 path) because tile sizes change and NCCL buffers are reallocated.

Samir: pasted trimmed perf report:
```
Timeline (nsight):
- t=0ms: batch assemble, kernel=matmul_fp16
- t=12ms: kernel_selector switches -> matmul_int8_reorder
- t=12.3ms: comm_temp alloc growth +600MB across ranks
- t=12.9ms: kv_staging copies +200MB
Peak memory owes ~+820MB transient per GPU
```
Correlates to batch boundary where short requests finish and long ones trigger different kernel variant.

Cheng: looks like two issues colliding: our kernel selection logic is eager (switch on smallest latency), and comm allocator assumes stable kernel footprint. When kernel changes we lose reuse and fall back to temp_alloc which races with workspace.

Alex: can we make kernel selection aware of memory churn? e.g., prefer slightly slower kernel if it prevents alloc storms.

Mira: prototyped a "stability penalty" in selector: if switching would increase transient mem > X% of free, bias towards current kernel unless expected latency win > threshold. Results on rig:
- stab_penalty=0.12: peak transient mem drops 270MB
- p95 latency increase negligible for stable workloads, p99 improved for mixed workloads

Samir: combined that with allocator tuning: change comm allocator to 1) a persistent slab for NCCL temp that is shared across kernel variants, 2) opportunistic reuse when kernel footprint shrinks, 3) delayed expand with async background growth. Pseudo policy:
```
acquire_comm(size):
  if slab.has(size): return slab.get(size)
  if free_mem_ratio > expand_thresh: slab.grow(size)
  else: fallback to temp_alloc (but enqueue async grow)
```
And background thread does slab.grow only if recent fallback count > churn_threshold.

Cheng: important: must not thrash between grow/shrink. We added 2s hysteresis and limit growth to 30% of initial slab per minute. Also added metric comm_slab.fallback_rate.

Alex: any KV cache interactions? when comm buffers shrink we might add more KV staging copies which hurts throughput.

Mira: ran KV-shard e2e: with new slab + selector stability
- KV copy count unchanged in steady state
- transient copy spikes reduced because comm buffers reused across kernels
- memory headroom improved by ~22% on mixed seq workloads

Samir: negative: sampling-heavy traces (many short-decisions) saw p50 jitter +6% due to rare background async grow. Tuned background grow to be rate-limited -> jitter down to +1.5%.

Cheng: opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2519 implementing selector stability + comm_slab manager + metrics (comm_slab.size_bytes, comm_slab.fallback_rate, kernel_selector.switch_score).

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for runtime:v3.9-selector-stable on cluster/infra-eu-central (6 nodes)

Mira: canary results so far (3h): no OOMs, comm_slab.fallback_rate ~0.02/s, mem.free_ratio avg +18%, p99 latency stable for long sequences, sampling p99 +0.9% (tuning ongoing).

Alex: next steps proposed:
1) extend perf harness to interleave kernel-variant heavy traces and short requests to stress the selector/allocator interaction
2) collect comm_slab.* + kernel_selector.* metrics for 48h in canary
3) add a Dedicated-only config to allow more aggressive slab sizes for tenants that opt-in
4) update rollout playbook: watch oom_count, comm_slab.fallback_rate, kernel_selector.switch_score, p99_latency_sampling

Samir: I'll add a synthetic workload that forces repeated kernel flip to ensure hysteresis prevents oscillation.

Cheng: agree. also add a safety cap so slab growth never consumes below workspace_reserved. policy: min_free_after_grow = workspace_reserved * 1.15.

Mira: pushing small tweak to default expand_thresh and the backoff for background grow. linking to test script: tools/ci/multi_kernel_mixture.sh

Alex: thanks team. big win if we can reduce these transient OOMs without hurting steady-state perf. ping ops-bot if canary alerts spike. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: monitor rule created: runtime/canary/selector-stable -> alert when oom_count>0 or comm_slab.fallback_rate>0.5/s for 5m

Samir: will post 12h AB summary in this thread once complete.
